# The sharp planar overlap coefficient for rank-two covers in every dimension

Let K be a convex body in R^d, d>=2, of volume V. Suppose three closed
halfspaces H_1,H_2,H_3 cover K and their normals span a space of dimension
at most two. Put A_i=vol_d(K intersect H_i). Then

    A_1+A_2+A_3-V >= (3/4)min_i A_i.                    (1)

Thus the dimension-dependent coefficients previously proved in
`candidate e239a5fb0d0efe4d` may all be
replaced by 3/4 under the same rank-two restriction. Their proofs remain
valid; the radialization below avoids their section-comparison loss.

## Proof

Rank one, a zero restricted normal, or a two-cap subcover is immediate:
if H_j,H_k cover K and i is the remaining index, then

    sum_l A_l-(3/4)min_l A_l >= V+A_i-(3/4)min_l A_l>=V.

For rank two let E be the normal span and D the orthogonal projection of
K onto E. The arbitrary-cover reduction proved in
`candidate 79c19cddb83423ea`
shows that either two original caps cover K, or the three projected
halfplanes cover the whole plane and their normals form a positive circuit.
Retain the latter case.

Their thresholds may be increased to concurrence at one point y in E,
as proved in Section 5 of the original overlap source. Write A_i'<=A_i
for the tightened cap masses. The functional

    F(A)=sum_i A_i-(3/4)min_i A_i

is coordinatewise nondecreasing, so it suffices to prove F(A')>=V.
If y is outside or on the boundary of D, the halfplane boundary lemma in
Section 3 of that source gives a two-cap subcover of D and the result is
again immediate.

Suppose y lies in int(D). If d=2, apply the already proved sharp ordinary
planar overlap theorem directly to K. If d>=3, let

    f(x)=vol_(d-2)(K intersect (x+E-perpendicular)),  x in E.

Fubini gives integral_E f=V and identifies the three tightened masses
with the integrals of f over their through-y halfplanes. Fiberwise
Brunn--Minkowski makes f^(1/(d-2)) concave on its positive support, so f
is log-concave. It is positive at y: any point of int(D) lifts to an
interior point of K and hence to a positive (d-2)-volume fiber.

The non-even radial-integral convexity lemma, Lemma 2 of
`candidate 0f025bdf9a51573b`, applies about ANY interior positive point;
it does not require a mode, centroid, or deepest point. Form the planar
Ball body B about y, written after translation to 0 as

    rho_B(v)^2=2 integral_0^infinity t f(y+t v)dt.

It is a convex body. Polar integration shows that its area is V and
that every through-origin halfplane has exactly the f-mass of the
corresponding through-y halfplane. The three concurrent halfplanes cover
the plane, so their traces on B have areas A_1',A_2',A_3'. The proved
ordinary PLANAR overlap theorem applied to B gives

    sum_i A_i'-(3/4)min_i A_i' >= |B|=V.

Monotonicity under the earlier tightening proves (1).

All original and tightened halfspaces are closed. They have zero d-volume
boundary before projection, and the projected density is absolutely
continuous, so all cap integrals and radial identities keep their exact
values. No affine map of the mixed lattice is being used.

## Scope and sharpness

The same proof works for any full-dimensional integrable log-concave
density on a plane: use its convex support in the cover reduction and its
Ball body about the concurrence point. Compact support is enough for the
application above; the cited radial lemma also treats unbounded integrable
log-concave densities.

The coefficient is sharp in every d>=2 within the rank-two class. Take
K=T x L, where T is a triangle and L is any (d-2)-dimensional convex body,
and use the three canonical centroid caps in the T coordinates. Each cap
has volume 4V/9 and the excess is V/3=(3/4)(4V/9). For d=2 omit L.

No claim about rank-three normal spans is made here. The new coefficient
is an ordinary continuous local fact; the unresolved arithmetic and
cross-fiber accounting in OC remain separate.
